Science.headline: In 1864, Tasmania introduced brown trout from England for sport; 162 years later...
Science.summary: In 1864, brown trout were introduced to Tasmania from England for recreational angling, an act now having profound ecological consequences 162 years later. Conservation workers are actively building barriers and clearing waterways to protect native Swan galaxias, a tiny fish species facing extinction due to the predatory brown trout. Efforts include creating trout-free refuges and relocating native fish, balancing angling traditions with critical species recovery.
key_points: Brown trout introduced to Tasmania in 1864 now threaten native fish species.
Conservationists are creating barriers and clearing waterways to save the endangered Swan galaxias.
Strategies include building trout-free refuges and relocating native fish.
The situation highlights the long-term ecological impact of introduced species.

key_points: Sea otters' return to a California estuary spurred significant ecological recovery.
Eelgrass coverage increased by 600%, enhancing marine habitats.
Marsh-edge erosion was reduced by 69%, stabilizing the environment.
The case highlights the positive impact of apex predator reintroduction on ecosystems.
